```python
remove = patch.place(zl_filter)[0]
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[2], pick.ins[1]),      # 1. the position
    (order.outs[1], black.ins[0]),     # 2. the notes to remove
    (black.outs[0], remove.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], every.ins[0]),     # 3. the list to filter
    (every.outs[0], remove.ins[0]),
    (remove.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),     # 60 62 64 65 67 69 71 72
    (pick.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.filter")
```

### `zl.group` (`zl_group`)

Store and output a list

**Collect notes into pairs.** zl.group 2 waits for two numbers, then sends them out together as one list. unpack splits each pair onto two oscillators, so random notes arrive as two-note chords.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, random, unpack, zl_group

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
pick = patch.place(random(13))[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
pair = patch.place(zl_group(2))[0]
split = patch.place(unpack(0, 0))[0]
hz_a, hz_b = patch.place(mtof, num_objs=2)
osc_a, osc_b = patch.place(cycle_tilde, num_objs=2)
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], pair.ins[0]),
    (pair.outs[0], split.ins[0]),
    (split.outs[0], hz_a.ins[0]),
    (split.outs[1], hz_b.ins[0]),
    (hz_a.outs[0], osc_a.ins[0]),
    (hz_b.outs[0], osc_b.ins[0]),
    (osc_a.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (osc_b.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.group")
```

### `zl.join` (`zl_join`)

Combine two lists

**Two phrases make one tune.** zl.join puts the list at its right inlet on the end of the list at its left. A rising phrase and a falling phrase join into one 8-note tune.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, trigger, zl_join, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "b", "i"))[0]
first = patch.place("message 60 64 67 72")[0]
second = patch.place("message 71 67 65 62")[0]
glue = patch.place(zl_join)[0]
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[2], pick.ins[1]),      # 1. the position
    (order.outs[1], second.ins[0]),    # 2. the end, stored at the right inlet
    (second.outs[0], glue.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], first.ins[0]),     # 3. the start, which sends the joined list
    (first.outs[0], glue.ins[0]),
    (glue.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.join")
```

### `zl.len` (`zl_len`)

Get list length

**Loop as long as the list.** zl.len counts the items in a list. Sent to counter as "max 5", the count makes the loop exactly as long as the melody, so editing the message box changes the loop too.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, prepend, trigger, zl_len, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 100))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
tune = patch.place("message 60 63 67 70 72")[0]
count = patch.place(zl_len)[0]
limit = patch.place(prepend("max"))[0]  # 5 -> "max 5" sets the counter's top
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], pick.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], tune.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], count.ins[0]),
    (count.outs[0], limit.ins[0]),
    (limit.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.len")
```

### `zl.median` (`zl_median`)

Get the median value of a list of numbers

**Smooth out random notes.** zl.median sends out the middle value of a list. zl.group gathers random notes in threes and only the middle one of each three plays, so the wildest notes are left out. Press ▶, then set the number box to 7 to take the middle of seven for a smoother line.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, number, random, zl_group, zl_median

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(120, active=1))[0]
pick = patch.place(random(25))[0]
three = patch.place(zl_group(3))[0]      # 3 numbers -> one list
size = patch.place(number)[0]            # a new group size
middle = patch.place(zl_median)[0]
note = patch.place("+ 55")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], three.ins[0]),
    (size.outs[0], three.ins[1]),
    (three.outs[0], middle.ins[0]),
    (middle.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.median")
```

### `zl.nth` (`zl_nth`)

Extract item from list

**Play a melody stored as a list.** zl.nth sends out the item at a position in a list, counting from 1. The counter steps that position from 1 to 8, so the message box plays as a tune.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, trigger, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]    # right first: the position, then the list
tune = patch.place("message 60 62 64 67 69 67 64 62")[0]
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], pick.ins[1]),      # position (cold inlet: stored)
    (order.outs[0], tune.ins[0]),      # then bang out the list
    (tune.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.nth")
```

### `zl.queue` (`zl_queue`)

Output elements of a list in the order they are received

**First in, first out.** zl.queue keeps the numbers it receives, and each bang sends out the oldest one. At the start of each bar the chord is queued, then one note leaves per beat, in the order they went in.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, iter_, metro, mtof, select, trigger, zl_queue

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
beat = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
bar = patch.place(select(0))[0]
chord = patch.place("message 60 64 67 72")[0]
each = patch.place(iter_)[0]             # one number at a time into the queue
fifo = patch.place(zl_queue)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], beat.ins[0]),
    (beat.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], bar.ins[0]),       # beat 0: refill the queue
    (bar.outs[0], chord.ins[0]),
    (chord.outs[0], each.ins[0]),
    (each.outs[0], fifo.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[0], fifo.ins[0]),      # every beat: take one out
    (fifo.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.queue")
```

### `zl.rev` (`zl_rev`)

Reverse a list

**A melody and its mirror.** zl.rev reverses a list. One voice plays the scale as written while a second plays the zl.rev copy, so the two move in opposite directions.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, trigger, zl_nth, zl_rev

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
tune = patch.place("message 60 62 64 65 67 69 71 72")[0]
back = patch.place(zl_rev)[0]
up = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
down = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz_up, hz_down = patch.place(mtof, num_objs=2)
osc_up, osc_down = patch.place(cycle_tilde, num_objs=2)
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], up.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[1], down.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], tune.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], up.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], back.ins[0]),
    (back.outs[0], down.ins[0]),       # 72 71 69 ... 60
    (up.outs[0], hz_up.ins[0]),
    (down.outs[0], hz_down.ins[0]),
    (hz_up.outs[0], osc_up.ins[0]),
    (hz_down.outs[0], osc_down.ins[0]),
    (osc_up.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (osc_down.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.rev")
```

### `zl.rot` (`zl_rot`)

Rotate a list

**A round from one list.** zl.rot shifts every item in a list along, wrapping the end round to the start. The second voice plays the tune rotated 2 places, so it follows the first 2 notes behind. Press ▶, then change the number box to set how far behind.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, number, trigger, zl_nth, zl_rot

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
tune = patch.place("message 60 62 64 65 67 65 64 62")[0]
shift = patch.place(zl_rot(2))[0]
places = patch.place(number)[0]          # a new rotation distance
lead = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
follow = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz_lead, hz_follow = patch.place(mtof, num_objs=2)
osc_lead, osc_follow = patch.place(cycle_tilde, num_objs=2)
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], lead.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[1], follow.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], tune.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], lead.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], shift.ins[0]),
    (places.outs[0], shift.ins[1]),
    (shift.outs[0], follow.ins[0]),
    (lead.outs[0], hz_lead.ins[0]),
    (follow.outs[0], hz_follow.ins[0]),
    (hz_lead.outs[0], osc_lead.ins[0]),
    (hz_follow.outs[0], osc_follow.ins[0]),
    (osc_lead.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (osc_follow.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.rot")
```

### `zl.slice` (`zl_slice`)

Slice a list in two

**Split a list into two voices.** zl.slice 4 sends the first 4 items out of its left outlet and the rest out of its right. The low half and the high half of the list play together as two voices.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, trigger, zl_nth, zl_slice

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 4))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
both = patch.place("message 48 53 55 52 64 65 67 64")[0]
split = patch.place(zl_slice(4))[0]
low = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
high = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz_low, hz_high = patch.place(mtof, num_objs=2)
osc_low, osc_high = patch.place(cycle_tilde, num_objs=2)
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], low.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[1], high.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], both.ins[0]),
    (both.outs[0], split.ins[0]),
    (split.outs[0], low.ins[0]),       # 48 53 55 52
    (split.outs[1], high.ins[0]),      # 64 65 67 64
    (low.outs[0], hz_low.ins[0]),
    (high.outs[0], hz_high.ins[0]),
    (hz_low.outs[0], osc_low.ins[0]),
    (hz_high.outs[0], osc_high.ins[0]),
    (osc_low.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (osc_high.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.slice")
```

### `zl.sort` (`zl_sort`)

Arrange a list in alphanumeric order

**Put the notes in order.** zl.sort sorts a list. The message box holds a scale in jumbled order; after zl.sort it plays as a rising scale. Press ▶, then set the number box to -1 to sort it falling instead.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, number, trigger, zl_nth, zl_sort

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
jumble = patch.place("message 67 60 72 64 69 62 71 65")[0]
sort = patch.place(zl_sort)[0]
direction = patch.place(number)[0]       # -1 falling, anything else rising
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], pick.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], jumble.ins[0]),
    (jumble.outs[0], sort.ins[0]),
    (direction.outs[0], sort.ins[1]),
    (sort.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.sort")
```

### `zl.stack` (`zl_stack`)

Output elements of a list in reverse order

**Last in, first out.** zl.stack keeps the numbers it receives, and each bang sends out the newest one. The chord goes in from the bottom up, so it comes back out from the top down.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, iter_, metro, mtof, select, trigger, zl_stack

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
beat = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
bar = patch.place(select(0))[0]
chord = patch.place("message 60 64 67 72")[0]
each = patch.place(iter_)[0]             # one number at a time onto the stack
lifo = patch.place(zl_stack)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], beat.ins[0]),
    (beat.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], bar.ins[0]),       # beat 0: refill the stack
    (bar.outs[0], chord.ins[0]),
    (chord.outs[0], each.ins[0]),
    (each.outs[0], lifo.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[0], lifo.ins[0]),      # every beat: take the top one off
    (lifo.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.stack")
```

### `zl.sum` (`zl_sum`)

Sum a list of numbers

**A scale from its steps.** zl.sum adds up a list. The message box holds the steps of a major scale; zl.slice keeps the first 1 to 8 of them, and their sum above 60 climbs the C major scale.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, trigger, zl_slice, zl_sum

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
steps = patch.place("message 0 2 2 1 2 2 2 1")[0]   # semitones between scale notes
first = patch.place(zl_slice(1))[0]
total = patch.place(zl_sum)[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], first.ins[1]),     # how many steps to keep
    (order.outs[0], steps.ins[0]),
    (steps.outs[0], first.ins[0]),
    (first.outs[0], total.ins[0]),
    (total.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("zl.sum")
```

## Data

Store values, tables and dictionaries.

### `coll` (`coll`)

Store and edit a collection of data

**Step through a stored melody.** coll stores a message at each address, and "next" sends out the next one, going back to the first after the last. listfunnel loads the melody as "0 67", "1 64" ... and the clock sends "next".

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import coll, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, listfunnel, loadbang, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
tune = patch.place("message 67 64 60 64 67 72 71 67")[0]
pairs = patch.place(listfunnel)[0]       # "address note" stores it
notes = patch.place(coll)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
advance = patch.place("message next")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], tune.ins[0]),
    (tune.outs[0], pairs.ins[0]),
    (pairs.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], advance.ins[0]),
    (advance.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (notes.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("coll")
```

### `table` (`table`)

Store and edit an array of numbers

**A melody in a table.** table holds a row of numbers: "set 0 60 63 ..." writes them from position 0 on, and a position at the left inlet reads one back. The counter reads positions 0 to 7, which plays the row as a tune.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, loadbang, metro, mtof, table

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
fill = patch.place("message set 0 60 63 65 67 70 67 65 63")[0]
notes = patch.place(table)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 7))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], fill.ins[0]),
    (fill.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (notes.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("table")
```

### `funbuff` (`funbuff`)

Store pairs of numbers

**Notes at a few points in time.** funbuff stores y values at x positions ("0 60" stores 60 at 0). Only 0, 2, 3 and 6 are stored here: at a step with nothing stored, funbuff answers with the one stored before it, so each note holds until the next.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, funbuff, loadbang, metro, mtof, trigger

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
fill = patch.place(trigger("b", "b", "b", "b"))[0]
points = [patch.place(f"message {x} {y}")[0] for x, y in [(0, 60), (2, 67), (3, 64), (6, 72)]]
notes = patch.place(funbuff)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 7))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], fill.ins[0]),
    *[(fill.outs[i], points[i].ins[0]) for i in range(4)],
    *[(p.outs[0], notes.ins[0]) for p in points],
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),      # an x alone reads its y
    (notes.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("funbuff")
```

### `bag` (`bag`)

Store a collection of numbers

**A bag of notes.** bag keeps every number it receives, and a bang sends them all out. At the start of each bar the bag empties its four notes into zl.queue, which plays one per beat.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import bag, counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, iter_, loadbang, metro, mtof, select, trigger, zl_queue

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
chord = patch.place("message 62 65 69 72")[0]
each = patch.place(iter_)[0]             # bag takes one number at a time
notes = patch.place(bag)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
beat = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
bar = patch.place(select(0))[0]
fifo = patch.place(zl_queue)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], chord.ins[0]),
    (chord.outs[0], each.ins[0]),
    (each.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], beat.ins[0]),
    (beat.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], bar.ins[0]),
    (bar.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),       # beat 0: bang empties the bag into the queue
    (notes.outs[0], fifo.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[0], fifo.ins[0]),      # every beat: play the next one
    (fifo.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("bag")
```

### `histo` (`histo`)

Create a histogram of numbers received

**Counting how often each note comes round.** histo counts how many times it has received each number. A counter steps through 0 to 3, played as a rising arpeggio on one sine; histo sends out how many times that step has now come round, and that count moves a low sine up a whole tone each time the arpeggio repeats (after six laps it starts again from the bottom).

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, histo, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
tally = patch.place(histo)[0]                 # left: the number, right: how many times so far
spread = patch.place("* 4")[0]
high = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
laps = patch.place("% 6")[0]
tone = patch.place("* 2")[0]
low = patch.place("+ 36")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof, num_objs=2)
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde, num_objs=2)
mix = patch.place("*~ 0.15")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], tally.ins[0]),
    (tally.outs[0], spread.ins[0]),
    (spread.outs[0], high.ins[0]),
    (high.outs[0], hz[0].ins[0]),
    (tally.outs[1], laps.ins[0]),
    (laps.outs[0], tone.ins[0]),
    (tone.outs[0], low.ins[0]),
    (low.outs[0], hz[1].ins[0]),
    (hz[0].outs[0], osc[0].ins[0]),
    (hz[1].outs[0], osc[1].ins[0]),
    (osc[0].outs[0], mix.ins[0]),
    (osc[1].outs[0], mix.ins[0]),
    (mix.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (mix.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("histo")
```

### `dict` (`dict_`)

Create and access dictionaries

**A dictionary as a memory.** At load, dict stores two pitches under the keys low and high. Every half second a get message asks for one of them; dict answers "low 220" or "high 330" from its second outlet, and route hands the number to the oscillator, so the tone swaps between 220 and 330 Hz.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_, ezdac_tilde, loadbang, metro, route, select

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
store_low = patch.place("message set low 220")[0]
store_high = patch.place("message set high 330")[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(500, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 1))[0]
pick = patch.place(select(0, 1))[0]
ask_low = patch.place("message get low")[0]
ask_high = patch.place("message get high")[0]
notes = patch.place(dict_("notes"))[0]
by_key = patch.place(route("low", "high"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], store_low.ins[0]),
    (start.outs[0], store_high.ins[0]),
    (store_low.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (store_high.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], ask_low.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[1], ask_high.ins[0]),
    (ask_low.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (ask_high.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (notes.outs[1], by_key.ins[0]),    # get answers "key value" here
    (by_key.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (by_key.outs[1], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict")
```

### `dict.pack` (`dict_pack`)

Create a dictionary and set its values

**Packing values into a dictionary.** dict.pack has an inlet for each key it names: freq and amp. Each new pitch from the counter arrives at the freq inlet, which sends the dictionary on; amp keeps its default of 0.2. dict.unpack takes the dictionary apart again, so you hear a rising scale of eight notes, over and over.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_pack, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(60, 67))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
pack = patch.place(dict_pack("freq:", "amp:", 0.2))[0]
unpack = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:", "amp:"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
level = patch.place("*~")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], pack.ins[0]),         # the freq inlet: sets freq and sends
    (pack.outs[0], unpack.ins[0]),     # "dictionary u…"
    (unpack.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),      # freq
    (unpack.outs[1], level.ins[1]),    # amp
    (osc.outs[0], level.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.pack")
```

### `dict.unpack` (`dict_unpack`)

Extract values from a dictionary

**Reading values out of a dictionary.** Two message boxes in dictionary syntax take turns: one loud and low, one quiet and high. dict.deserialize turns each into a dictionary, and dict.unpack sends the value of freq out of its first outlet and amp out of its second, so the tone alternates between a loud 220 Hz and a softer 440 Hz.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro, select

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(400, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 1))[0]
pick = patch.place(select(0, 1))[0]
loud = patch.place("message freq: 220 amp: 0.25")[0]
soft = patch.place("message freq: 440 amp: 0.08")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
unpack = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:", "amp:"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
level = patch.place("*~")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], loud.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[1], soft.ins[0]),
    (loud.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (soft.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], unpack.ins[0]),     # "dictionary u…"
    (unpack.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),      # freq
    (unpack.outs[1], level.ins[1]),    # amp
    (osc.outs[0], level.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.unpack")
```

### `dict.route` (`dict_route`)

Compare dictionaries

**Sorting dictionaries.** Four dictionaries take turns, each with a side and a pitch. dict.route compares each one with its argument, side: left. The ones that match leave by the left outlet and play in your left ear; the others leave by the right outlet and play in your right ear.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_route, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro, select

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
pick = patch.place(select(0, 1, 2, 3))[0]
first = patch.place("message side: left freq: 262")[0]
second = patch.place("message side: right freq: 330")[0]
third = patch.place("message side: left freq: 392")[0]
fourth = patch.place("message side: right freq: 523")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
sort = patch.place(dict_route("side:", "left"))[0]
left_freq = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:"))[0]
right_freq = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:"))[0]
left_osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
right_osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
left_quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
right_quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], first.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[1], second.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[2], third.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[3], fourth.ins[0]),
    (first.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (second.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (third.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (fourth.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], sort.ins[0]),
    (sort.outs[0], left_freq.ins[0]),   # side is left
    (sort.outs[1], right_freq.ins[0]),  # anything else
    (left_freq.outs[0], left_osc.ins[0]),
    (right_freq.outs[0], right_osc.ins[0]),
    (left_osc.outs[0], left_quiet.ins[0]),
    (right_osc.outs[0], right_quiet.ins[0]),
    (left_quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (right_quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.route")
```

### `dict.iter` (`dict_iter`)

Stream the content of a dictionary

**A chord from a dictionary.** Each dictionary holds three notes under the keys root, third and fifth. dict.iter sends its entries out one at a time as "key value" lists, and route sends each note to its own oscillator, so you hear a C major chord change to an F major chord and back.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_iter, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, route, select

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(1000, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 1))[0]
pick = patch.place(select(0, 1))[0]
c_major = patch.place("message root: 60 third: 64 fifth: 67")[0]
f_major = patch.place("message root: 65 third: 69 fifth: 72")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
each = patch.place(dict_iter)[0]
by_key = patch.place(route("root", "third", "fifth"))[0]
hz = [patch.place(mtof)[0] for _ in range(3)]
osc = [patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0] for _ in range(3)]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.1")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], c_major.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[1], f_major.ins[0]),
    (c_major.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (f_major.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], each.ins[0]),
    (each.outs[0], by_key.ins[0]),     # "root 60", "third 64", "fifth 67"
    *[(by_key.outs[i], hz[i].ins[0]) for i in range(3)],
    *[(hz[i].outs[0], osc[i].ins[0]) for i in range(3)],
    *[(osc[i].outs[0], quiet.ins[0]) for i in range(3)],
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.iter")
```

### `dict.join` (`dict_join`)

Merge the content of two dictionaries

**Adding keys to a dictionary.** dict.join merges two dictionaries: the one arriving on the left, and the one on the right, here set by its arguments to amp: 0.15. Each step makes a dictionary holding only freq; after dict.join it holds amp as well, and dict.unpack sets both the pitch and the level of a sine.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_join, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(4, 8))[0]
hz = patch.place("* 55")[0]
text = patch.place("message freq: $1")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
join = patch.place(dict_join("amp:", 0.15))[0]
unpack = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:", "amp:"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
level = patch.place("*~")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], join.ins[0]),
    (join.outs[0], unpack.ins[0]),
    (unpack.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),      # freq
    (unpack.outs[1], level.ins[1]),    # amp, from dict.join's arguments
    (osc.outs[0], level.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.join")
```

### `dict.strip` (`dict_strip`)

Remove keys from a dictionary

**Taking a key out of a dictionary.** dict.strip removes the keys it names, here amp, from each dictionary that passes: the removed key and its value go out the right outlet, and the dictionary without it out the left. route amp keeps the level, which sets the volume, while freq from the rest sets the pitch.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_strip, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro, route

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(4, 8))[0]
hz = patch.place("* 55")[0]
text = patch.place("message freq: $1 amp: 0.2")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
strip = patch.place(dict_strip("amp"))[0]
amp = patch.place(route("amp"))[0]
unpack = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
level = patch.place("*~")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], strip.ins[0]),
    (strip.outs[1], amp.ins[0]),       # "amp 0.2", taken out
    (amp.outs[0], level.ins[1]),
    (strip.outs[0], unpack.ins[0]),    # the dictionary without amp
    (unpack.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], level.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.strip")
```

### `dict.serialize` (`dict_serialize`)

Convert a dictionary's content to text

**A dictionary as text, and back.** dict.serialize writes a dictionary out as dictionary syntax, freq : 330, the same text a message box could hold; dict.deserialize reads that text back into a dictionary. Each step goes through the round trip, and the frequency that comes out the far end plays.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_serialize, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(4, 8))[0]
hz = patch.place("* 55")[0]
text = patch.place("message freq: $1")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
write = patch.place(dict_serialize)[0]
read = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
unpack = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], write.ins[0]),
    (write.outs[0], read.ins[0]),      # "freq : 330"
    (read.outs[0], unpack.ins[0]),
    (unpack.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.serialize")
```

### `dict.deserialize` (`dict_deserialize`)

Create a dictionary from text

**Text into a dictionary.** dict.deserialize reads dictionary syntax, key, colon, value, and makes a dictionary of it. The counter steps 4 to 8; times 55 that is 220 to 440 Hz; the message box puts it after "freq:" ($1 is the number that arrived); dict.unpack takes freq back out, and a sine plays it.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, dict_deserialize, dict_unpack, ezdac_tilde, metro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(4, 8))[0]
hz = patch.place("* 55")[0]
text = patch.place("message freq: $1")[0]
make = patch.place(dict_deserialize)[0]
unpack = patch.place(dict_unpack("freq:"))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], make.ins[0]),
    (make.outs[0], unpack.ins[0]),     # "dictionary u…"
    (unpack.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),      # freq
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dict.deserialize")
```

### `fromsymbol` (`fromsymbol`)

Convert a symbol into numbers/messages

**Numbers from text.** fromsymbol reads a symbol as a message: the text "60 64 67 72" becomes four numbers again. Here tosymbol makes the text, and after fromsymbol zl.nth can pick the notes out one by one.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, fromsymbol, metro, mtof, tosymbol, trigger, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 4))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
numbers = patch.place("message 60 64 67 72")[0]
text = patch.place(tosymbol)[0]          # one item: the text "60 64 67 72"
back = patch.place(fromsymbol)[0]        # four items: 60 64 67 72
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], pick.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], numbers.ins[0]),
    (numbers.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], back.ins[0]),
    (back.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("fromsymbol")
```

### `tosymbol` (`tosymbol`)

Convert messages, numbers, or lists to a single symbol

**Hear the digits.** tosymbol turns a whole message into one symbol, the text "60 64 67". atoi then gives the character code of each digit and space (6 is 54, a space 32), and those codes play as a tune.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import atoi, counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, tosymbol, trigger, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 8))[0]     # "60 64 67" is 8 characters
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
numbers = patch.place("message 60 64 67")[0]
text = patch.place(tosymbol)[0]
codes = patch.place(atoi)[0]
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
note = patch.place("+ 12")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], pick.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], numbers.ins[0]),
    (numbers.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], codes.ins[0]),
    (codes.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("tosymbol")
```

### `atoi` (`atoi`)

Convert characters to integers

**Play a word.** atoi turns a word into the character code of each letter: "hello" becomes 104 101 108 108 111. Less 36, those codes are notes, and zl.nth plays them in turn.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import atoi, counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, trigger, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(1, 5))[0]
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
word = patch.place("message hello")[0]
codes = patch.place(atoi)[0]
pick = patch.place(zl_nth(1))[0]
note = patch.place("- 36")[0]            # h = 104 -> 68
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], pick.ins[1]),
    (order.outs[0], word.ins[0]),
    (word.outs[0], codes.ins[0]),
    (codes.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("atoi")
```

### `itoa` (`itoa`)

Convert character codes to symbol

**Type a number, character by character.** itoa turns character codes into text: 54 is the digit 6 and 48 to 55 are 0 to 7, so "54 48" becomes the text "60". fromsymbol reads that text as the number 60, and the notes climb from 60 to 67.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, fromsymbol, itoa, metro, mtof, prepend

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
digit = patch.place(counter(48, 55))[0]  # the codes of 0 .. 7
codes = patch.place(prepend(54))[0]      # the code of 6 in front: "54 48"
text = patch.place(itoa)[0]              # -> the text "60"
number = patch.place(fromsymbol)[0]      # -> the number 60
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], digit.ins[0]),
    (digit.outs[0], codes.ins[0]),
    (codes.outs[0], text.ins[0]),
    (text.outs[0], number.ins[0]),
    (number.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("itoa")
```

### `spell` (`spell`)

Convert input to UTF-8 (Unicode) codes

**Spell a word out in notes.** spell sends the character code of each letter of a word: "hello" gives 104 101 108 108 111. At the start of each word they go into zl.queue, and one letter plays per beat.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, select, spell, trigger, zl_queue

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
beat = patch.place(counter(0, 4))[0]     # five letters
order = patch.place(trigger("b", "i"))[0]
start = patch.place(select(0))[0]
word = patch.place("message hello")[0]
letters = patch.place(spell)[0]
fifo = patch.place(zl_queue)[0]
note = patch.place("- 36")[0]            # h = 104 -> 68
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], beat.ins[0]),
    (beat.outs[0], order.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[1], start.ins[0]),     # beat 0: spell the word into the queue
    (start.outs[0], word.ins[0]),
    (word.outs[0], letters.ins[0]),
    (letters.outs[0], fifo.ins[0]),
    (order.outs[0], fifo.ins[0]),      # every beat: play the next letter
    (fifo.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("spell")
```

### `match` (`match`)

Watch for a message match, then output the message

**Ring a bell on a pattern.** match 7 0 waits for the numbers 7 then 0 in a row and sends them out when they come. The counter goes 7 then 0 each time it starts over, so a high bell rings at the top of every bar.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, line_tilde, match, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 7))[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
tune = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
spot = patch.place(match(7, 0))[0]
strike = patch.place("message 1 5 0 600")[0]
env = patch.place(line_tilde)[0]
bell = patch.place(cycle_tilde(1568))[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], tune.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], spot.ins[0]),
    (spot.outs[0], strike.ins[0]),
    (strike.outs[0], env.ins[0]),
    (bell.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (env.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (tune.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("match")
```

### `anal` (`anal`)

Make a histogram of number pairs

**Count how often a step repeats.** anal reports each pair of numbers in a row, with how many times that pair has come so far: "previous current count". The counter loops 0 1 2 3, so every pair comes once more each round, and the count, played as pitch, climbs a step each round.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import anal, counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, zl_nth

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
pairs = patch.place(anal)[0]
count = patch.place(zl_nth(3))[0]        # the third item: the count
higher = patch.place("* 2")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 58")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], pairs.ins[0]),
    (pairs.outs[0], count.ins[0]),
    (count.outs[0], higher.ins[0]),
    (higher.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("anal")
```

## Random

Chance and variation.

### `random` (`random`)

Generate a random number

**Random notes.** random outputs a number from 0 up to (not including) its argument each time it gets a bang: here 0..23, shifted up to MIDI notes 48..71.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, random

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
pick = patch.place(random(24))[0]
shift = patch.place("+ 48")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], shift.ins[0]),
    (shift.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("random")
```

### `drunk` (`drunk`)

Output random numbers within a step range

**A random walk.** drunk moves a random step (up to 3) from where it was, within 0..23, so the melody wanders instead of jumping.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import drunk, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, tri_tilde

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(150, active=1))[0]
walk = patch.place(drunk(24, 3))[0]
shift = patch.place("+ 55")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(tri_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], walk.ins[0]),
    (walk.outs[0], shift.ins[0]),
    (shift.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("drunk")
```

### `urn` (`urn`)

Generate random numbers without duplicates

**Shuffle, no repeats.** urn 8 picks 0 to 7 at random but never the same number twice. When all 8 are used it bangs its right outlet, and "clear" refills it: each run of 8 notes plays every note of the scale once, in a new order.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof, urn

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
bag = patch.place(urn(8))[0]
refill = patch.place("message clear")[0]
step = patch.place("* 2")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], bag.ins[0]),
    (bag.outs[1], refill.ins[0]),      # all used: refill
    (refill.outs[0], bag.ins[0]),
    (bag.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("urn")
```

### `decide` (`decide`)

Choose randomly between 1 and 0

**Flip a coin.** decide outputs 0 or 1 at random on each bang. Times 12 plus 57, that picks between two A's an octave apart, every 200 ms.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, decide, ezdac_tilde, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
coin = patch.place(decide)[0]
octave = patch.place("* 12")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 57")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], coin.ins[0]),
    (coin.outs[0], octave.ins[0]),
    (octave.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("decide")
```

## MIDI

Notes and controllers.

### `makenote` (`makenote`)

Generate a note-on/note-off pair

**Notes with a length.** makenote pairs each pitch with a velocity (100) and sends a matching note-off (velocity 0) 200 ms later. Divided by 127, the velocity drives adsr~: up to start the note, 0 to end it.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import adsr_tilde, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, makenote, metro, mtof, random

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(400, active=1))[0]
pick = patch.place(random(12))[0]
shift = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
notes = patch.place(makenote(100, 200))[0]   # velocity, duration ms
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
level = patch.place("/ 127.")[0]             # velocity 0..127 -> 0..1
env = patch.place(adsr_tilde(5, 80, 0.6, 150))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]              # times the envelope (silent until it rises)
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], pick.ins[0]),
    (pick.outs[0], shift.ins[0]),
    (shift.outs[0], notes.ins[0]),
    (notes.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),        # pitch
    (notes.outs[1], level.ins[0]),     # velocity
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], env.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (env.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("makenote")
```

### `stripnote` (`stripnote`)

Filter out note-off messages

**Drop the note-offs.** stripnote passes a pitch only when the velocity in its right inlet is not 0. decide gives each step velocity 100 or 0 (a note-off), so only some steps of the scale pluck; the rest are rests.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, decide, ezdac_tilde, line_tilde, metro, mtof, stripnote

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(200, active=1))[0]
order = patch.place("t b b")[0]
coin = patch.place(decide)[0]
velocity = patch.place("* 100")[0]
step = patch.place(counter(60, 67))[0]
ons = patch.place(stripnote)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
pluck = patch.place("message 1 5 0 180")[0]
env = patch.place(line_tilde)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], order.ins[0]), (order.outs[1], coin.ins[0]), (coin.outs[0], velocity.ins[0]),
    (velocity.outs[0], ons.ins[1]), (order.outs[0], step.ins[0]), (step.outs[0], ons.ins[0]),
    (ons.outs[0], hz.ins[0]), (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]), (ons.outs[1], pluck.ins[0]),
    (pluck.outs[0], env.ins[0]), (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]), (env.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("stripnote")
```

### `flush` (`flush`)

Output MIDI note-offs for held notes

**Let go of every held note.** flush remembers each note-on that passes through it. These notes never get a note-off, so the tone never stops; every 2.25 seconds a bang makes flush send a note-off (velocity 0) for each, and the tone drops out until the next note.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, flush, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(500, active=1))[0]
release = patch.place(metro(2250, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(60, 64))[0]
note_on = patch.place("t i 100")[0]   # velocity first (right), then the pitch
held = patch.place(flush)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
level = patch.place("/ 127.")[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]), (step.outs[0], note_on.ins[0]),
    (note_on.outs[1], held.ins[1]), (note_on.outs[0], held.ins[0]),
    (release.outs[0], held.ins[0]),
    (held.outs[0], hz.ins[0]), (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (held.outs[1], level.ins[0]), (level.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("flush")
```

### `notein` (`notein`)

Receive MIDI note messages

**Notes from a MIDI keyboard.** notein outputs the pitch and velocity of each key you play. Play a MIDI keyboard to change the pitch and loudness; until then cycle~ holds its 262 Hz (middle C) at a fixed level.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, mtof, notein

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
keys = patch.place(notein)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
level = patch.place("/ 127.")[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.5")[0]        # until a velocity arrives
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (keys.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),         # pitch
    (keys.outs[1], level.ins[0]),      # velocity: 0 when the key is let go
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("notein")
```

### `ctlin` (`ctlin`)

Output received MIDI control values

**A knob on your controller.** ctlin outputs the value (0 to 127) of any knob, fader or mod wheel you move. Play a MIDI keyboard's mod wheel, or turn a knob, to open and close the filter on this buzzing saw~; until then lores~ holds it at 600 Hz.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import ctlin, ezdac_tilde, lores_tilde, saw_tilde, scale

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
knob = patch.place(ctlin)[0]
cutoff = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 200, 4000))[0]
buzz = patch.place(saw_tilde(110))[0]
filt = patch.place(lores_tilde(600, 0.5))[0]   # cutoff Hz, resonance
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (knob.outs[0], cutoff.ins[0]),
    (cutoff.outs[0], filt.ins[1]),
    (buzz.outs[0], filt.ins[0]),
    (filt.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("ctlin")
```

### `bendin` (`bendin`)

Output MIDI pitch bend values

**The pitch-bend wheel.** bendin outputs the bend wheel's position, 0 to 127 with 64 in the middle. Minus 64, divided by 32, that's up to 2 semitones either way around note 60. Play a MIDI keyboard's bend wheel to bend the tone; until then it holds middle C.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import bendin, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
wheel = patch.place(bendin("a", 1))[0]   # port a, channel 1
centre = patch.place("- 64")[0]
semis = patch.place("/ 32.")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60.")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (wheel.outs[0], centre.ins[0]),
    (centre.outs[0], semis.ins[0]),
    (semis.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("bendin")
```

### `pgmin` (`pgmin`)

Receive MIDI program changes

**Program changes pick the note.** pgmin outputs the program number (1 to 128) when you choose a preset on your instrument. % 12 plus 60 turns it into a note. Play a MIDI keyboard's program or preset buttons to change the pitch; until then cycle~ holds middle C.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, mtof, pgmin

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
preset = patch.place(pgmin("a", 1))[0]   # port a, channel 1
fold = patch.place("% 12")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (preset.outs[0], fold.ins[0]),
    (fold.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("pgmin")
```

### `midiparse` (`midiparse`)

Interpret raw MIDI data

**Read raw MIDI.** midiparse sorts raw MIDI bytes by type: notes come out its left outlet as "pitch velocity". Here midiformat makes the bytes for random notes, so no device is needed, and unpack takes the pitch for the oscillator.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, metro, midiformat, midiparse, mtof, pack, random, unpack

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
pick = patch.place(random(12))[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
pair = patch.place(pack(0, 100))[0]    # pitch, velocity
raw = patch.place(midiformat)[0]
parse = patch.place(midiparse)[0]
split = patch.place(unpack(0, 0))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], pick.ins[0]), (pick.outs[0], note.ins[0]), (note.outs[0], pair.ins[0]),
    (pair.outs[0], raw.ins[0]), (raw.outs[0], parse.ins[0]),
    (parse.outs[0], split.ins[0]),     # note: pitch velocity
    (split.outs[0], hz.ins[0]), (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]), (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("midiparse")
```

### `midiformat` (`midiformat`)

Prepare data in the form of a MIDI message

**Write raw MIDI.** midiformat turns numbers into MIDI bytes; its third inlet makes control changes from "controller value". A counter sweeps controller 74 from 0 to 127, and midiparse reads it back to open the filter on a saw~.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, ezdac_tilde, lores_tilde, metro, midiformat, midiparse, prepend, saw_tilde, scale, unpack

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(20, active=1))[0]
sweep = patch.place(counter(0, 127))[0]
cc = patch.place(prepend(74))[0]       # "74 value"
raw = patch.place(midiformat)[0]
parse = patch.place(midiparse)[0]
split = patch.place(unpack(0, 0))[0]
cutoff = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 200, 3000))[0]
buzz = patch.place(saw_tilde(110))[0]
filt = patch.place(lores_tilde(600, 0.5))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], sweep.ins[0]), (sweep.outs[0], cc.ins[0]),
    (cc.outs[0], raw.ins[2]),          # third inlet: control change
    (raw.outs[0], parse.ins[0]),
    (parse.outs[2], split.ins[0]),     # control: number value
    (split.outs[1], cutoff.ins[0]), (cutoff.outs[0], filt.ins[1]),
    (buzz.outs[0], filt.ins[0]),
    (filt.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]), (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("midiformat")
```

## Interface

Knobs, sliders and buttons, played from the patch.

### `slider` (`slider`)

Move a slider to output values

**Drag to change the pitch.** A slider sends 0..127 as you drag it. scale maps that onto 200..1000 Hz for cycle~. Press ▶, then drag the slider in the patch.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, scale, slider

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
knob = patch.place(slider)[0]
hz = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 200, 1000))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(330))[0]     # 330 Hz until you move the slider
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (knob.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("slider")
```

### `dial` (`dial`)

Output numbers using an onscreen dial

**Turn a dial to open a filter.** A dial sends 0..127 as you turn it. scale maps that onto a cutoff of 200..4000 Hz for lores~, which filters a buzzy saw~. Press ▶, then drag the dial up and down: the sound gets brighter and darker.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import dial, ezdac_tilde, lores_tilde, saw_tilde, scale

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
knob = patch.place(dial)[0]
cutoff = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 200, 4000))[0]
saw = patch.place(saw_tilde(110))[0]
filt = patch.place(lores_tilde(600, 0.7))[0]   # 600 Hz until you turn the dial
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (knob.outs[0], cutoff.ins[0]),
    (cutoff.outs[0], filt.ins[1]),       # middle inlet: the cutoff
    (saw.outs[0], filt.ins[0]),
    (filt.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("dial")
```

### `kslider` (`kslider`)

Output numbers from an onscreen keyboard

**Play notes on a keyboard.** kslider is a piano keyboard: clicking a key sends its MIDI note number. mtof turns it into hertz for cycle~, which a metro plucks four times a second. Press ▶, then click the keys of the kslider to change the note.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, kslider, line_tilde, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
keys = patch.place(kslider)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]     # middle C until you click a key
clock = patch.place(metro(250, active=1))[0]
shape = patch.place("message 1 5 0 200")[0]
env = patch.place(line_tilde)[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (keys.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),           # left outlet: the note; right: velocity
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], shape.ins[0]),
    (shape.outs[0], env.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (env.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("kslider")
```

### `nslider` (`nslider`)

Output numbers from a notation display

**Choose a note on the staff.** nslider shows a note on a musical staff and sends its MIDI note number when you change it. mtof turns the note into hertz for tri~. Press ▶, then change the note in the nslider (60 is middle C) to change the pitch.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import ezdac_tilde, mtof, nslider, tri_tilde

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
staff = patch.place(nslider)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(tri_tilde(262))[0]       # middle C until you pick a note
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (staff.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("nslider")
```

### `rslider` (`rslider`)

Display or change a range of numbers

**Stretch an interval.** rslider selects a range and sends both ends: the low end from its left outlet, the high end from its right. Each end sets the pitch of one cycle~, so the two notes are the range. Press ▶, then drag either end of the rslider to pull the notes apart or together.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, mtof, rslider, scale

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
ends = patch.place(rslider)[0]
low = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 48, 72))[0]    # 0..127 -> MIDI notes C3..C5
high = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 48, 72))[0]
low_hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
high_hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc_low = patch.place(cycle_tilde(220))[0]
osc_high = patch.place(cycle_tilde(330))[0]    # a fifth above, until you drag
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.1")[0]           # two tones add up: keep each quieter
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (ends.outs[0], low.ins[0]),
    (ends.outs[1], high.ins[0]),
    (low.outs[0], low_hz.ins[0]),
    (high.outs[0], high_hz.ins[0]),
    (low_hz.outs[0], osc_low.ins[0]),
    (high_hz.outs[0], osc_high.ins[0]),
    (osc_low.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (osc_high.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("rslider")
```

### `multislider` (`multislider`)

Display data as sliders or a scrolling display

**A volume fader.** multislider is a row of sliders that sends all their values as a list; this one has a single slider, set to 0..1. It sets the volume of cycle~ through *~. Press ▶, then drag the multislider to the bottom to silence the tone and to the top for full volume.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
fader = patch.place(mp.MaxObject("multislider", setminmax=[0., 1.]))[0]   # Max's default is -1..1
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(330))[0]
level = patch.place("*~ 0.5")[0]           # half volume until you move it
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (fader.outs[0], level.ins[1]),
    (osc.outs[0], level.ins[0]),
    (level.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("multislider")
```

### `number` (`number`)

Display and output numbers, lists, and messages

**Type a note number.** A number box holds a whole number and sends it when it changes. Here it is a MIDI note: mtof turns it into hertz for tri~. Press ▶, then drag up and down on the number box, or click it and type a note (60 is middle C, 72 an octave up).

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import ezdac_tilde, mtof, number, tri_tilde

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
note = patch.place(number)[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(tri_tilde(262))[0]       # middle C until you set a number
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("number")
```

### `flonum` (`flonum`)

Display and output a number

**Set the speed of a tremolo.** flonum is a number box for decimals. It sets the rate, in hertz, of a slow cycle~ that swells the volume of a tone up and down. Press ▶, then type 0.5 into the flonum for a slow swell or 12 for a fast flutter.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, flonum

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
rate = patch.place(flonum)[0]
lfo = patch.place(cycle_tilde(4))[0]       # 4 swells a second until you change it
depth = patch.place("*~ 0.5")[0]
offset = patch.place("+~ 0.5")[0]          # -1..1 becomes 0..1, a volume
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(330))[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (rate.outs[0], lfo.ins[0]),
    (lfo.outs[0], depth.ins[0]),
    (depth.outs[0], offset.ins[0]),
    (offset.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("flonum")
```

### `toggle` (`toggle`)

Switch between off and on (0 and 1)

**Switch up an octave.** A toggle is an on/off switch: clicking it sends 1, clicking again sends 0. * 12 and + 57 turn that into MIDI note 57 or 69, an octave apart. Press ▶, then click the toggle to jump between the two notes.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, mtof, toggle

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
switch = patch.place(toggle)[0]
octave = patch.place("* 12")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 57")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(220))[0]     # note 57, the toggle's "off"
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (switch.outs[0], octave.ins[0]),
    (octave.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("toggle")
```

### `button` (`button`)

Blink and send a bang

**Click to pluck.** A button sends a bang when clicked, and flashes whenever a bang passes through it. Here metro bangs it twice a second and each bang plucks a note. Press ▶ to watch it flash, then click the button to add notes of your own.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import button, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, line_tilde, metro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(500, active=1))[0]
hit = patch.place(button)[0]
shape = patch.place("message 1 5 0 300")[0]
env = patch.place(line_tilde)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(440))[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], hit.ins[0]),
    (hit.outs[0], shape.ins[0]),
    (shape.outs[0], env.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (env.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("button")
```

### `message` (`message`)

Send any message

**Click a message to change the note.** A message box sends what it says when you click it. These three send 262, 330 and 392, the hertz of C, E and G, to cycle~. Press ▶, then click the message boxes to play a chord one note at a time.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
c = patch.place("message 262")[0]
e = patch.place("message 330")[0]
g = patch.place("message 392")[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (c.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (e.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (g.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("message")
```

### `umenu` (`umenu`)

Pop-up menu

**Choosing notes from a menu.** umenu is a pop-up menu: choosing an item sends its number (from 0) out the left outlet and its text, as a message, out the middle one. At load the menu is cleared and given the items 60, 64, 67 and 72, and the counter chooses each in turn, so the menu's notes play as a C major arpeggio.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, loadbang, metro, mtof, trigger, umenu

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
steps = patch.place(trigger("b", "b", "b", "b", "b"))[0]   # fires right to left
empty = patch.place("message clear")[0]
c = patch.place("message append 60")[0]
e = patch.place("message append 64")[0]
g = patch.place("message append 67")[0]
c2 = patch.place("message append 72")[0]
menu = patch.place(umenu)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
choose = patch.place(counter(0, 3))[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], steps.ins[0]),
    (steps.outs[4], empty.ins[0]),
    (steps.outs[3], c.ins[0]),
    (steps.outs[2], e.ins[0]),
    (steps.outs[1], g.ins[0]),
    (steps.outs[0], c2.ins[0]),
    (empty.outs[0], menu.ins[0]),
    (c.outs[0], menu.ins[0]),
    (e.outs[0], menu.ins[0]),
    (g.outs[0], menu.ins[0]),
    (c2.outs[0], menu.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], choose.ins[0]),
    (choose.outs[0], menu.ins[0]),
    (menu.outs[1], hz.ins[0]),       # the item's text: a MIDI note
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("umenu")
```

### `tab` (`tab`)

Tab control

**Tabs that pick an octave.** tab is a row of buttons: choosing one sends its number (from 0) out the left outlet and its text out the middle one. loadbang names the tabs low, mid and high, and the clock chooses each in turn, so a tone climbs an octave at a time, then drops back to the lowest.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, loadbang, metro, mtof, tab

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
names = patch.place("message tabs low mid high")[0]
tabs = patch.place(tab)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(500, active=1))[0]
choose = patch.place(counter(0, 2))[0]
octave = patch.place("* 12")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 57")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde)[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], names.ins[0]),
    (names.outs[0], tabs.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], choose.ins[0]),
    (choose.outs[0], tabs.ins[0]),
    (tabs.outs[0], octave.ins[0]),   # the tab's number: 0, 1, 2
    (octave.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("tab")
```

### `radiogroup` (`radiogroup`)

Radio button or check box

**Pick a harmonic.** radiogroup is a column of buttons of which one is on; clicking one sends its number, from 0 at the top. + 1 and * 110 turn 0..3 into 110, 220, 330 and 440 Hz, the first four harmonics of A. Press ▶, then click the radiogroup's buttons to step up the series.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
# four buttons, in a box tall enough to show them (16 px each), in Max and here
choice = patch.place(mp.MaxObject("radiogroup", size=4, patching_rect=[0.0, 0.0, 18.0, 66.0]))[0]
harmonic = patch.place("+ 1")[0]
hz = patch.place("* 110")[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(110))[0]     # the top button's note
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (choice.outs[0], harmonic.ins[0]),
    (harmonic.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("radiogroup")
```

### `incdec` (`incdec`)

Increment and decrement a value

**Step through the semitones.** incdec is a pair of arrows: each click adds or subtracts 1 and sends the new number. + 60 makes it a MIDI note counted from middle C, and mtof turns that into hertz. Press ▶, then click the up and down arrows to walk the pitch one semitone at a time.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, incdec, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
arrows = patch.place(incdec)[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]     # middle C until you click
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (arrows.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("incdec")
```

### `matrixctrl` (`matrixctrl`)

Matrix switch control

**A grid of notes.** matrixctrl is a grid of switches; clicking a cell sends the list "column row value". Like a guitar neck, each column is a semitone up and each row a fourth up, counted from C3. Press ▶, then click cells in the matrixctrl to play their notes.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, mtof, unpack

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
grid = patch.place(mp.MaxObject("matrixctrl", columns=8, rows=8))[0]
cell = patch.place(unpack(0, 0))[0]        # keeps column and row, drops the value
fourths = patch.place("* 5")[0]
add = patch.place("+ 0")[0]                # column + 5 * row
note = patch.place("+ 48")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(131))[0]     # note 48 until you click
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (grid.outs[0], cell.ins[0]),
    (cell.outs[1], fourths.ins[0]),      # unpack sends right to left: the row first
    (fourths.outs[0], add.ins[1]),
    (cell.outs[0], add.ins[0]),
    (add.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("matrixctrl")
```

### `pictslider` (`pictslider`)

Picture-based slider control

**Two controls in one.** pictslider moves in two directions at once: left-right is sent from its left outlet, up-down from its right, each 0..127. Here left-right sets the pitch of saw~ and up-down the cutoff of lores~. Press ▶, then move the pictslider's two controls.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import ezdac_tilde, lores_tilde, pictslider, saw_tilde, scale

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
pad = patch.place(pictslider)[0]
pitch = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 55, 220))[0]
bright = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 200, 4000))[0]
saw = patch.place(saw_tilde(110))[0]
filt = patch.place(lores_tilde(800, 0.7))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (pad.outs[0], pitch.ins[0]),
    (pad.outs[1], bright.ins[0]),
    (pitch.outs[0], saw.ins[0]),
    (bright.outs[0], filt.ins[1]),
    (saw.outs[0], filt.ins[0]),
    (filt.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("pictslider")
```

### `led` (`led`)

Color on/off button
