**A light on the beat.** led lights up when it receives a number other than 0 and goes dark at 0. counter alternates 0 and 1 on every metro tick, which lights the led and also picks the higher of two notes. Press ▶ and watch the led light on each high note.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import counter, cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, led, metro, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
clock = patch.place(metro(300, active=1))[0]
step = patch.place(counter(0, 1))[0]
light = patch.place(led)[0]
fifth = patch.place("* 7")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], step.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], light.ins[0]),
    (step.outs[0], fifth.ins[0]),
    (fifth.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("led")
```

### `comment` (`comment`)

Explanatory note or label

**Label a patch.** A comment is text in the patch, for the people reading it: it has no outlets and makes no sound. This one tells you what to do with the slider beside it. Press ▶, then drag the slider as the comment says.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, scale, slider

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
note = patch.place("comment drag the slider to change the pitch")[0]
knob = patch.place(slider)[0]
hz = patch.place(scale(0, 127, 200, 800))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(330))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (knob.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("comment")
```

### `panel` (`panel`)

Colored background area

**A coloured background.** panel draws a filled rectangle. It has no outlets and makes no sound; in Max you put it behind a group of objects to set them apart. Press ▶ to hear the patch beside it, a metro plucking a note.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, line_tilde, metro, panel

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
background = patch.place(panel)[0]
clock = patch.place(metro(400, active=1))[0]
shape = patch.place("message 1 5 0 300")[0]
env = patch.place(line_tilde)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(392))[0]
amp = patch.place("*~ 0.")[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (clock.outs[0], shape.ins[0]),
    (shape.outs[0], env.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], amp.ins[0]),
    (env.outs[0], amp.ins[1]),
    (amp.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("panel")
```

### `key` (`key`)

Report keyboard presses

**Play with your computer keyboard.** key sends the code of each key you press on the computer keyboard. % 12 folds every code into one octave, + 60 starts it at middle C, and mtof turns it into hertz. Press ▶, then press keys on your keyboard: each key plays its own note.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, key, mtof

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
keys = patch.place(key)[0]
fold = patch.place("% 12")[0]
note = patch.place("+ 60")[0]
hz = patch.place(mtof)[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(262))[0]     # middle C until you press a key
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (keys.outs[0], fold.ins[0]),
    (fold.outs[0], note.ins[0]),
    (note.outs[0], hz.ins[0]),
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("key")
```

### `keyup` (`keyup`)

Report key information on release

**Hold a key for a higher note.** keyup sends a key's code when you let go of it, where key sends it when you press. Pressing any key sends 440 to cycle~ and letting go sends 220. Press ▶, then hold down any key on your keyboard and release it.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, key, keyup

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
down = patch.place(key)[0]
up = patch.place(keyup)[0]
high = patch.place("message 440")[0]
low = patch.place("message 220")[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(220))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (down.outs[0], high.ins[0]),         # any message makes a message box send
    (up.outs[0], low.ins[0]),
    (high.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (low.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("keyup")
```

## Video

Jitter: camera input and simple image processing.

### `jit.grab` (`jit_grab`)

Digitize video from an external source

**Your camera in the patch.** jit.grab reads frames from a camera. In Max it needs an "open" message to start the camera and a bang for each frame, which qmetro sends 30 times a second; jit.pwindow shows the frames. Allow camera access, then press ▶ to see yourself.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import jit_grab, jit_pwindow, loadbang, qmetro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]     # turn the camera on
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]   # one frame every 33 ms
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
screen = patch.place(jit_pwindow)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], screen.ins[0]),
)
patch.save("jit_grab")
```

### `jit.matrix` (`jit_matrix`)

The Jitter Matrix!

**Pixelate the camera.** jit.matrix holds a picture of a fixed size. Copying the camera into one only 40 by 30 pixels big, then showing it full size in jit.pwindow, makes big square pixels. Allow camera access, then press ▶ and wave at the camera.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import jit_grab, jit_matrix, jit_pwindow, loadbang, qmetro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
small = patch.place(jit_matrix(4, "char", 40, 30))[0]   # 4 planes of char, 40 x 30 pixels
screen = patch.place(jit_pwindow)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], small.ins[0]),
    (small.outs[0], screen.ins[0]),
)
patch.save("jit_matrix")
```

### `jit.window` (`jit_window`)

Display data in a window

**Show the camera in a window.** jit.window displays frames; in Max it opens a window of its own outside the patch, and here it is drawn in the patch. Allow camera access, then press ▶ to see the camera.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import jit_grab, jit_window, loadbang, qmetro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
window = patch.place(jit_window)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], window.ins[0]),
)
patch.save("jit_window")
```

### `jit.pwindow` (`jit_pwindow`)

Display Jitter data and images

**A picture inside the patch.** jit.pwindow draws each frame it receives inside the patch, and passes the frame on from its left outlet, so a second jit.pwindow can show it again further down. Allow camera access, then press ▶ to see the camera in both.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import jit_grab, jit_pwindow, loadbang, qmetro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
first = patch.place(jit_pwindow)[0]
second = patch.place(jit_pwindow)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], first.ins[0]),
    (first.outs[0], second.ins[0]),      # the frame passes through
)
patch.save("jit_pwindow")
```

### `jit.brcosa` (`jit_brcosa`)

Adjust image brightness/contrast/saturation

**A black-and-white camera.** jit.brcosa changes a picture's brightness, contrast and saturation; 1 leaves each one as it is. Here saturation 0 takes out the colour and contrast 1.5 makes it punchier. Allow camera access, then press ▶.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import jit_brcosa, jit_grab, jit_pwindow, loadbang, qmetro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
grade = patch.place(jit_brcosa(brightness=1.1, contrast=1.5, saturation=0))[0]
screen = patch.place(jit_pwindow)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], grade.ins[0]),
    (grade.outs[0], screen.ins[0]),
)
patch.save("jit_brcosa")
```

### `jit.scalebias` (`jit_scalebias`)

Multiply and add

**Fade the camera to grey.** jit.scalebias multiplies each colour by its scale, then adds its bias (colours run 0 to 1): rscale, gscale and bscale 0.5 halve the contrast, and rbias, gbias and bbias 0.25 lift the darks, so the picture looks washed out. (Its plain scale and bias apply only in channel-summing mode, mode 1.) Allow camera access, then press ▶.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import jit_grab, jit_pwindow, jit_scalebias, loadbang, qmetro

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
fade = patch.place(jit_scalebias(rscale=0.5, gscale=0.5, bscale=0.5,
                                 rbias=0.25, gbias=0.25, bbias=0.25))[0]   # each colour: 0.5 * in + 0.25
screen = patch.place(jit_pwindow)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], fade.ins[0]),
    (fade.outs[0], screen.ins[0]),
)
patch.save("jit_scalebias")
```

### `jit.3m` (`jit_3m`)

Report min/mean/max values

**A webcam theremin.** jit.3m measures each frame: the minimum, mean and maximum of each plane (alpha, red, green, blue, 0 to 255), out its left, middle and right outlets. Here the mean's green value, the one that follows brightness most closely, is scaled to 150..900 Hz for cycle~. Allow camera access, press ▶, then cover the camera with your hand to lower the pitch, or turn towards a light to raise it.

```python
import maxpylang as mp
from maxpylang.objects import cycle_tilde, ezdac_tilde, jit_3m, jit_grab, loadbang, qmetro, scale, unpack

patch = mp.MaxPatch()
start = patch.place(loadbang)[0]
open_ = patch.place("message open")[0]
clock = patch.place(qmetro(33, active=1))[0]
camera = patch.place(jit_grab)[0]
measure = patch.place(jit_3m)[0]
planes = patch.place(unpack(0., 0., 0., 0.))[0]    # alpha, red, green, blue
hz = patch.place(scale(0., 255., 150, 900))[0]
osc = patch.place(cycle_tilde(300))[0]
quiet = patch.place("*~ 0.2")[0]
out = patch.place(ezdac_tilde)[0]

patch.connect(
    (start.outs[0], open_.ins[0]),
    (open_.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (clock.outs[0], camera.ins[0]),
    (camera.outs[0], measure.ins[0]),
    (measure.outs[1], planes.ins[0]),  # the mean of each plane
    (planes.outs[2], hz.ins[0]),       # green
    (hz.outs[0], osc.ins[0]),
    (osc.outs[0], quiet.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[0]),
    (quiet.outs[0], out.ins[1]),
)
patch.save("jit_3m")
```

---

# API reference

Generated from the docstrings in the `maxpylang` package. Import with `import maxpylang as mp`.

## `mp.MaxPatch(template=None, load_file=None, reorder=True, verbose=True)`

```text
This class represents a MaxMSP patch. A MaxPatch can be created as a copy of a template file, or by loading in an existing *.maxpat* file.

:param template: the path to a template *.maxpat* file. Can be given as an absolute path, a relative path from the current directory, or a relative path from ``MaxPy/maxpy/data/PATCH_TEMPLATES/``.
:type template: str, optional; default: None

:param load_file: the path to an existing *.maxpat* file to be loaded in. Can be given as an absolute path or a relative path from the current directory.
:type load_file: str, optional; default: None

:param reorder: whether or not to reassign object ids after loading in an existing file. See :func:`MaxPatch.reorder`.
:type reorder: bool, optional; default: True

:param verbose: for logging output.
:type verbose: bool, optional; default: True
```

### `MaxPatch.objs` (property)

```text
A dictionary of all Max objects in the patch, stored by object id. Read-only.
```

### `MaxPatch.num_objs` (property)

```text
The number of Max objects in the patch. Read-only.
```

### `MaxPatch.curr_position` (property)

```text
The current position of the 'cursor' at which to place Max objects. Given as a two-element list [x, y] of patch coordinates.
Can be set using :func:`MaxPatch.set_position`.
```

### `MaxPatch.dict` (property)

```text
The JSON dict of the patch. Read-only.
```

### `MaxPatch.place(*objs, randpick=False, num_objs=1, seed=None, weights=None, spacing_type='grid', spacing=[80.0, 80.0], starting_pos=None, verbose=False)`

```text
Place objects in the patch.

        objs --> list of object names as strings, OR list of objects as prev. created MaxObjects (or mix of both)
    randpick --> True: pick n random objs from objs list (default pick 1)
          - num_objs --> integer: n = num_objs
          - num_objs --> list: give error & take first element on list
          - num_objs --> None: n = len(objs)
    randpick --> False: pick all objs on objs list (default each picked once)
          - num_objs --> integer: each obj multiplied by num_objs
          - num_objs --> list: each objs multiplied by corresponding num_objs entry
          - num_objs --> None: n = len(objs)
        seed --> random seed for picking/placing objs, if None then random seed
     weights --> weight probabilities for picking objs, if None then equal probability
spacing_type --> options for how to place objs on canvas
          - "grid": objects centered on a grid
                - spacing --> tuple/list length 2: [x, y] grid spacings
          - "random": random locations, using same seed as before (overlaps possible)
                - spacing --> N/A
          - "custom": location specified for each object
                - spacing --> list: positions [[x, y]], can only be used for num_objs=1
          - "vertical": objects stacked vertically
                - spacing --> number: specify height
starting_pos --> starting position to place from, must be tuple/list length 2: [x, y]

verbose --> print output for seed, etc.

:returns: a list of the MaxObjects that have been created
```

### `MaxPatch.set_position(new_x, new_y, from_place=False, verbose=False)`

```text
Set the current "cursor" position from which objects will be placed.

Must be formatted as [x, y] tuple or int of length 2. 
```

### `MaxPatch.connect(*connections, verbose=True)`

```text
This method creates patchcords to connect objects. *currently fixing connection specification...*

:param \*connections: a list of connections to make. Each connection must be specified as a tuple (:class:`~maxpy.Outlet`, :class:`~maxpy.Inlet` (, ``list``)). The optional third element specifies midpoints (curves) of the patchcord as a list of [x, y] coordinates.

:param verbose: for logging output.
:type verbose: bool, optional; default: True

:returns: None
```

### `MaxPatch.save(filename='default.maxpat', device_type=None, verbose=True, check=True)`

```text
Save to .maxpat or .amxd file.

Usage:
filename --> savefile name (.maxpat or .amxd)
device_type --> for Max for Live .amxd files: "instrument", "audio_effect", or "midi_effect"
                required when saving as .amxd; when set, forces .amxd extension
verbose --> print log message to console
check --> check the patch once it is written: unknown objects, js and abstraction links,
          cords, and the shape of the patch (GraphWarning for a hot loop, audio feedback
          with no delay, or output that reaches nothing)
```

### `MaxPatch.replace(curr_obj_num: str, new_obj, retain=True, verbose=False, **new_attribs)`

```text
Replace an object in the patch with a different object. 

The new object can be specified as a string, or by reference to a MaxObject.
Attributes in common (i.e. common box attribs) between old/new objects can be retained (will automatically retain).  
Additional attribute settings will override retained attributes.
Patchcords will automatically be retained if possible, starting from xlet 0. 

curr_obj_num --> id number in 'obj-num' string format of current object to be replaced
new_obj --> either string specification or MaxObject of new object
retain --> retain all attributes in common between old/new objects
verbose --> log to console
new_attribs --> any new attributes to give to the new object
```

### `MaxPatch.delete(objs=None, cords=None, verbose=True)`

```text
Delete objects and/or patchcords.
Deleting objects will automatically delete any patchcords attached to them.

 objs --> list of string "obj-num" objects to delete
cords --> list of connections (Outlet, Inlet)
```

### `MaxPatch.reorder(verbose=False)`

```text
Re-number objects in patch, starting from 1. 
```

### `MaxPatch.inspect(*objs, info='all')`

```text
Get desired information about specified objects.

   objs --> list of objs to get info about, as strings "obj-num"
       - if objs="all", print info for each object
   info --> desired info to print out 
       - "all": print all info below
       - "canvas": print obj-num, position, connections to each inlet/outlet
       - 
       - "attributes": print current settings of all available attributes
       - "common-box": print current settings of common box attributes, if applicable
       - "obj-attribs": print current settings of obj-specific attributes, if applicable
       -
       - "connections": print connections to each inlet/outlet
       - "position": print position on canvas 
```

### `MaxPatch.check(*flags, device_type=None)`

```text
This method checks the patch for linked abstractions, unknown objects, linked/unlinked js objects,
cords that send audio into an inlet that takes no audio, and problems in the shape of the
patch: hot loops, audio feedback with no delay, and outputs that reach nothing.

:param \*flags: takes keywords ``'abstractions'``, ``'unknowns'``, ``'js'``, ``'cords'``. If no flags given,
    checks all five categories. ``'graph'`` checks the shape of the patch.
:param device_type: the Max for Live device type the patch is saved as, if any. Inside a
    device, dac~ and ezdac~ are not outputs.
:type \*flags: str, optional

:returns: outputs a list of all the objects that fall under the specified categories, identified by object id, name, text, and linked file (if applicable).
:rtype: printed output
```

## `mp.MaxObject(text, from_dict=False, abstraction=False, inlets=None, outlets=None, **extra_attribs)`

```text
This class represents a Max object within a Max patch.

To create a *cycle~* object with a frequency of 440 Hz, you would use the in-box text: ``"cycle~ 440"``.     
You can also include attributes in the in-box text by using the '@' symbol followed by the attribute name and value. For example, to create a *jit.movie* object that loads the file *crashtest.mov*, you would use the in-box text: ``"jit.movie @moviefile crashtest.mov"``.
TODO: this seems to not work for UI objects maybe. 
Objects have inlets and outlets, which are accessible via the ``.ins`` and ``.outs`` properties, respectively. You can access individual inlets and outlets by indexing into these lists. For example, to access the first outlet of an object named *myobj*, you would use ``myobj.outs[0]``.
```

```text
Initialize a MaxObject.

from_dict = False --> initialize from in-box text (normal initialization in Max env)
    text --> in-box text
    extra_attribs --> attributes to change, formatted as attribute_name = val

from_dict = True --> initialize from given json dict representation of obj (for loading in from existing file)
    text --> json dict
    extra_attribs --> not used

abstraction = True --> treat as abstraction without needing the .maxpat file in cwd
    inlets --> number of inlets (default 0)
    outlets --> number of outlets (default 0)
```

### `MaxObject.name` (property)

```text
The name of the MaxObject, e.g. 'sel', 'bang', 'js'.
```

### `MaxObject.ins` (property)

```text
A list of Inlet objects attached to the MaxObject.
```

### `MaxObject.outs` (property)

```text
A list of Outlet objects attached to the MaxObject.
```

### `MaxObject.__call__(*args, **attribs)`

```text
Make a new object of the same class with in-box arguments and attributes.

``cycle_tilde(440)`` is ``MaxObject("cycle~ 440")``, and
``metro(500, active=1)`` is ``MaxObject("metro 500 @active 1")``.
```

### `MaxObject.edit(text_add='append', text=None, **extra_attribs)`

```text
Edit an object by adding/replacing text and specifying attributes. 

text_add --> 'append' : keep current args/text attributes, append specified args/text attributes
text_add --> 'replace': erase current args/text attributes, replace with specified args/text attributes

Should not use this function to change object class (i.e. name)!!!
Can only change args/text attributes/extra attributes
```

### `MaxObject.move(x, y)`

```text
Move an object to the specified location. 
```

### `MaxObject.link(link_file=None)`

```text
Link a file for a js object or abstraction.

link_file --> the filename, file MUST be placed in current directory
link_file = None --> for js object with prev. given filename, will try to link that again
                 --> otherwise, won't work

For js objects, linking or re-linking will automatically update the text field to reflect the proper filename.
```

### `MaxObject.inspect()`

```text
Print out specified information about the object. 
```

### `MaxObject.notknown()`

```text
Return true if the object has no ref_file.
```

Class representing MaxObject Inlet. 

Generic over the rate it accepts (see maxpylang.rates), for static checking only.

Keeps track of patchcords through a list of source Outlets.
Also keeps track of midpoints of the cord, if any. 
```

```

```

```

## `mp.import_objs(*packages, overwrite=False, defaults='max')`

```text
Import objects from MaxMSP packages for compatibility with Python interface.
Creates object template files.

Requires io files for each package describing the relationship between inlets/outlets and arguments.

Usage:
input --> list of package folder names, use keyword "vanilla" as shortcut for [max, msp, jit, m4l]. 
overwrite --> flag to re-import previously imported objects 
defaults --> where each object's default box comes from:
    "max": Max opens a patch of bare objects and saves it. Needs an authorized Max,
           because an unauthorized one cannot save.
    "shipped": read from the patches Max ships (help files and examples), which Max
           saved itself. Needs no running Max. An estimate: see get_shipped_obj_info
           for how a box is chosen and how far it agrees with a Max save.

With defaults="max", make sure the Max application is OPEN when running this command!
If import fails, set wait_time higher and re-import. 
```

## `mp.DEVICE_TYPES`

The `device_type` values `save()` and `save_amxd()` accept: `"audio_effect"`, `"midi_effect"`, `"instrument"`.

## `maxpylang.rates`

```text
Rates: what travels on a patch cord, as seen by a static type checker.

Inlets and outlets are generic over a rate, so ``Outlet[Signal]`` is an audio
outlet and ``Inlet[Control]`` is an inlet that only takes messages. A checker
such as ty or mypy then rejects ``patch.connect((osc.outs[0], flonum.ins[0]))``.

These classes are markers only and are never instantiated.

    Control  --> messages: numbers, symbols, lists, bang
    Matrix --> a Jitter matrix; it travels as a message, so it is a Control
    Signal --> MSP audio
    MCSignal --> multichannel audio; legal wherever a Signal is

Control into an audio inlet is always allowed, because most audio inlets also
take messages (``start``, a float for a constant). Only Signal into an inlet
that takes no audio is rejected.
```

## `maxpylang.exceptions.UnknownObjectWarning`

```text
Raised when a Max object name is not recognized.
```
